quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Broken yellow lines are used on streets and highways to:

options.text: Mark no passing zones.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to give more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car or from between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their car without seeing you.

questions.question: For a person 21 years or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol in drivers under age 21. Any amount of alcohol in your system will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed because they are larger and heavier. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your side of the road. Do not use your bright lights in return.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means that:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the way ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow traffic light. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the light turns red.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow centerline means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow centerline means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, you should always:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep your speed the same.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When approaching a roundabout, slow down. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
Do not turn left.
Do not make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn left.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is illegal and unsafe to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The highest speed you can drive is 55 mph when conditions are good.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest speed you can drive is 55 mph when conditions are good.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed limit for this road. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. You must follow the speed limit.

questions.question: You are leaving the interstate. When should you start slowing down?

options.text: Halfway through the exit lane.
As you get near the exit lane.
Right when you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed the same until you enter the exit lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check if other drivers are entering the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other drivers. Never pass or change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Once you clear the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This makes sure you have enough space to safely pull in front.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Drive at the same speed as in dry conditions.
Brake hard as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road in wet conditions. Your car rides on water instead of the road surface. The best way to prevent this is to drive more slowly in rain or wet weather.

questions.question: You should always drive at:

options.text: The same speed as the vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should depend on road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger car.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than cars. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams will reflect back at you and create glare, making it hard to see.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around and go the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You are parked uphill on a street with a curb. After setting the parking brake, what should you do with the front wheels?

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parked uphill without a curb or when parked downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light means the red light is coming. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through the intersection as quickly and safely as you can.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: This sign means a railroad crossing is ahead without signals. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, look both ways and listen for trains. Be ready to stop if you see or hear a train coming. Never try to go faster than a train to cross.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the brake pedal.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: When a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using the brakes lightly. Do not stop on the road if possible. Pull off safely.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection ahead, and you have not entered it yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: At a yellow light, stop your vehicle safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
At the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: How can you avoid the glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright glare from oncoming headlights. After a quick glance to the side, look ahead again to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Enter the intersection halfway to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter the intersection unless you can drive all the way across.
Drive into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection unless you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even if your light is green, do not enter the intersection unless you can get completely through before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: A school bus is picking up or dropping off children. What must you do?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are going the same direction as the bus.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must stop completely before reaching the bus. This applies regardless of the direction you are traveling.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Drive farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
Stay no more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in the mirrors. The driver will not know you are there. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety space if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent will:

options.text: Have no effect on your driving.
Not put other drivers at risk.
Double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles a driver's risk of being in a fatal crash.

questions.question: When visibility is less than 100 feet due to bad weather, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Pull off the road and wait for the weather to clear.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and wait for the weather to clear.
questions.explanation: Heavy rain, heavy snow, or thick fog can limit your vision to less than 100 feet ahead. You cannot drive safely in these conditions at any speed. If you cannot see well enough to drive safely, pull off the road.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in residential areas unless a different speed is posted?

options.text: 20 mph
30 mph
45 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in residential areas is 30 mph. If a different speed limit is posted, follow the posted limit.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to watch for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to watch for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for potential hazards. Staring only at the road directly ahead is dangerous. Scan the road ahead and watch the vehicles around you.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this road sign?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign means a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What do signs with orange backgrounds mean?

options.text: General warning signs
Construction and maintenance warning signs
Regulatory signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction and maintenance warning signs
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on secondary highways unless a different speed is posted?

options.text: 55 mph
60 mph
70 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 70 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit on secondary highways is 70 mph. If a different speed limit is posted, follow the posted limit.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on roadways. You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign. Do not proceed until the intersection is clear and you can safely pass through.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles
Where signs and pavement markings allow passing
On a curve with no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and pavement markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections or at entrances to parking lots and alleys. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead. Assume an oncoming vehicle is hidden from view. Only pass where signs and markings permit it, and only if you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because your car needs a quarter mile to stop.
To keep up with traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles entering at on-ramps and be ready for quick changes in road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not need the full lane
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder
Keep your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane. Never share the same lane with a motorcycle. If you return to your lane too soon, you may force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When passing, move back to the right lane when:

options.text: You are one vehicle length ahead of the other car
You can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror
You are 50 feet ahead of the other car

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Only pass if you have enough room to return safely. Make sure you have enough space between your car and the car you passed. When both headlights appear in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing
Pedestrian crossing
Jogging trail

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a place where pedestrians cross. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students exit the bus
The stop arm is raised
The stop arm is raised and the bus starts moving

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is raised and the bus starts moving
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights and its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped. Do not move until the red lights stop, the stop arm is raised, and the bus drives away.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes means:

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction
You can pass when it is safe
You cannot pass

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes going opposite directions. You can pass if there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills
Follow other vehicles closely to maintain traction
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills
questions.explanation: Use a low gear before going down a steep hill to prevent skidding. Keep more distance between you and the car ahead than usual. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes if you do not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: The speed limit in business areas is:

options.text: 20 mph
30 mph
45 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in business areas is 30 mph unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow posted signs if they show a different limit.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most traffic
Stay within that speed range
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (within posted limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot collide. Multi-vehicle crashes happen when some cars go faster or slower than others.
